marketBrief.headline: Oil eases as Wall Street looks to Big Tech and the Fed
marketBrief.summary: U.S. futures point to a modestly higher open after oil retreated from a six-month high. The bounce is conditional: investors are entering a Fed decision week alongside earnings from the largest cloud platforms and data releases that will test growth and inflation.
bullets: S&P 500 futures were up 0.4% and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.7%, Bloomberg reported; CNBC had Dow futures 209 points higher.
Brent traded at $115.02 and WTI at $101.01 in CNBC's Monday premarket update, both lower, but still elevated.
Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday after the close; Amazon follows Thursday, keeping AI spending and cloud growth in focus.
The Federal Reserve's two-day meeting ends Wednesday; a near-5% 10-year yield remains a headwind for borrowing costs and long-duration valuations.
Thursday at 8:30 a.m. ET brings the advance Q3 GDP estimate and September personal income/outlays; the BLS Employment Cost Index follows Friday morning.

calendar.why: Consumer demand and Boeing's aircraft production and certification outlook provide a read on staples and aerospace.
A volatile measure of factory demand can update the growth picture just ahead of the Fed decision.
The statement can move short-term rate expectations, the dollar, Treasury yields and equity valuations.
Cloud growth and AI infrastructure spending are central to whether investors accept the buildout's cost.

calendar.event: Q3 GDP advance estimate and September Personal Income and Outlays (including PCE inflation)
calendar.why: The releases combine a first estimate of quarterly growth with the Fed's preferred inflation gauges.
AWS growth and infrastructure investment are a key read on AI cloud demand and monetization.
Compensation trends help markets assess services inflation and labor-cost pressure.
Control of Congress can reshape expectations for taxes, regulation and fiscal policy; results arrive through the evening.
Payrolls, unemployment and wage data will shape expectations for the Fed's next steps.
The CPI inflation report is a key cross-check on the inflation trend after the Fed meeting.
